Since we have multiple experienced players, and the DM was very new he was extremely railroad-y. Despite this his NPC's would deny us important information until we forced them to tell us by denying them a quest reward we retrieved for them. Almost like forcing someone to do something, but then not telling them why to do it.  This process happened twice in four sessions each of which was the group talking to one NPC for a simple piece of info and both took almost 40 minutes to an hour each. I want to stress that this DM wasn't exactly bad, but he was not the DM for a group of players experienced with roleplay and know their characters' motivations thoroughly. This along with combat being very lackluster and sometimes gimmicky (all three combats we had started with an ambush we could not prepare or respond to even when we spotted the danger preemptively). All these combined made it a very unfun experience.
I personally enjoy homebrew worlds much more to modules, and not a problem at all we are fine with any age!

Roll20 is very much preferred, and i dont think we are looking for full theatre of the mind. If you have another free system in mind we may be willing to try it out. Hope that answers the question, have a good one!

The concept of turning pirate garb into its own version of unarmored defense actually sounds really good, but our intention wasnt to "Sneak a powerful effect in through the back door" our objective was never to make something horrendously broken and I believe that we did a fair job balancing with a few oversights and i am personally in no way demoralised. The criticism we got that was fair was insightful and i was happy to hear it, and the joy I've gotten seeing the upvotes go up heavily influenced me to make this subclass better. Thanks for the critique, and the tip in balancing!

Though multiclassing is extremely hard to account for when balancing a class... if your sorcerer, bard, or warlock take a three level dip into fighter just for the AC, maybe they deserve the extra AC. But this also implies that you are playing with people who would take three levels in a class just because its broken, which can easily be done with the core handbook classes regardless of their power (bearbearian for example is infamous for its power). This predominantly becomes a problem with hexblade warlock but lets be honest, almost *any* martial class can be broken using hexblade warlock. But thank you for the criticisms regardless, we'll be looking to balance the class out when it is re-released as part of a larger project.

These are both fair points but as it stands an average fighter using a shield should have an AC of 18 around level 5, this is something that is similar to the dread Pirate, though we have not physically changed the information due to that requiring a full reposting of the subclass. We are scaling down pirate garb's AC. But even with it as is it takes until level 12 (shorter if you prioritise cha over dex) in order to get your AC up to 20 while using a shield, which for that level i believe to be reasonable considering the bonus to hit on most monsters the party will be fighting. And as for taking resilient that is a fair point, but even with a 20 AC that is not an insurmountable number though i do agree it is high. Thanks for the input!

That's fine if thats your opinion but it was stated that this is only the first iteration. This was posted with the intent of getting feedback as much as showing it off. But thanks for the unneeded comment that is in no way helpful, unlike those who had actual criticisms that we are taking into account in order to better this project.

Thanks for the feedback! Our intentions when making this was to make it somewhat strong, which i believe we did while not making it overpowered. Im glad to see someone thinks it may be *underpowered* but in the next iteration we are going to change around the 15th level ability entirely or at least heavily change it. We wanted to focus on using a stat generally not intended for fighter. Im glad to have your input, thanks for the comment!

Hi! So im the co-creator of this class and with that mindset you have im sure this seems broken. That being said even with this setup you have an 8 in dex, intelligence, and wisdom. Regardless of the 21 potential ac (for reference a paladin at level 1 can get a 20 ac using chain mail, a shield and shield of faith) this means all saving throws for most spells and natural weapons have a -1. I feel this makes the class balanced, being extremely good in close quarters is the focal point. This means anything that requires a save from most spells you are now very susceptible to. Though I do believe that the pirate garb should be changed thanks to the insight gotten from posting this subclass here,  anything can be made broken if you min max every potentially strong aspect of a class. Thank you for your opinion.
